figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Representative xanthone natural products and proposed mechanisms of anthraquinone ring cleavage. (a) Representative xanthone natural
products. The xanthone scaffold is highlighted in red. (b) Proposed Baeyer−Villiger oxidation mechanism for the formation of cephalanone F. (c)
Proposed reductive mechanism for the formation of cephalanone F by an NADPH-dependent reductase and an atypical nonheme iron-dependent
dioxygenase. (d) Previously proposed mechanism for the C4a−C10 bond cleavage of 1a in c.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Catalytic pocket of BTG13 and the optimized geometry of
the BTG13/1a/O2 complex (E·S·O2)I. (a) The catalytic pocket of the
most representative snapshot from the MD simulations. (b) The
optimized structure of the lowest-energy BTG13/1a/O2 complex (E·
S·O2)I in this study. The atoms colored green are fixed in the
quantum chemical calculations. (c) Detailed interaction network
between the active site of BTG13 and 1a. Key distances are given in
Å. Most of the nonpolar hydrogen atoms are hidden for clarity.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Tautomerization between 1a and 1b tautomers. (a) Energy profile and optimized geometries of key intermediates and transition states of
BTG13-mediated tautomerization from 1a to 1b. (b) Energy profile of water-mediated tautomerization from 1a to 1b. All energies are given in
kcal/mol. Nonpolar hydrogen atoms and residue H185 are hidden for clarity. Key distances are given in Å.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Energy and structural analysis of the first two steps of the C−C bond cleavage mechanism of the anthrone form 1a. (a) Energy profiles of
the first two step reactions at the quintet, singlet (open shell), triplet, and septet state. All energies are given in kcal/mol. (b) Spin natural orbitals
and orbital diagrams of quintet state (E·S·O2)I. (c) Optimized geometries of the intermediates involved in the first two steps of the reaction and the
key distances at the quintet state (septet state in parentheses for comparison). Nonpolar hydrogen atoms and residue H185 are hidden for clarity.
Key distances are given in Å.

figure_candidates.label: Scheme 1
figure_candidates.caption: Scheme 1. Three Potential C−C Bond Cleavage Mechanisms of the Anthrone Form 1a

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Energy profile for the most favorable pathway of C−C bond cleavage of 1a (path I-a) and the key intermediates and transition states. (a)
Energy profiles and schematic drawings of the intermediates for the oxygen radical attacking on C4a (path I-a, colored in black) and C10a (path I-R,
colored in yellow). All energies are given in kilocalories per mole. (b) Optimized geometries of key intermediates and transition states. Nonpolar
hydrogen atoms and residue H185 are hidden for clarity. Key distances are given in Å.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. CC bond cleavage mechanisms starting from the naphthol form 1b. (a) Simplified schematic drawings of two CC bond cleavage
mechanisms. (b) Energy profiles and schematic drawings of key intermediates for the CC bond cleavage starting from naphthol form 1b. All
energies are relative to those of (E·S·O2)I and are given in kcal/mol.

figure_candidates.label: Scheme 2
figure_candidates.caption: Scheme 2. Full C−C Bond Cleavage Mechanism of the Substrate Catalyzed by BTG13 Proposed in This Study

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Catalytic details for the first two steps of the C−C bond cleavage pathway of 1a when BTG13 bears different axial ligands. (a, b) The
optimized geometries of (E·S·O2)I bearing Kcx (a) and Lys (b). Key distances, spin densities in the quintet (septet) state, the amount of charge
transferred from the ligand to the iron center (ΔqCT), and the quintet-septet energy gap (ΔEQ‑S) are labeled. Nonpolar hydrogen atoms and residue
H185 are hidden for clarity. Key distances are given in Å. (c) Energy profiles for the first two steps of the C−C bond cleavage pathway of 1a from
7(E·S·O2)I to 5TS2I bearing different axial ligands in BTG13. All energies are relative to 7(E·S·O2)I. (d) Correlation between the quintet−septet
energy gap (ΔEQ‑S) and the ionization potential of the respective ligands. (e) The amount of charge transferred from the ligand to the iron center
(ΔqCT) and the quintet−septet energy gap (ΔEQ‑S). Energies are given in kcal/mol.
